source: Public Citizen/AFR report (NAIC data) via Inman

headline: Premiums up 59%,
payouts *just 28%*
slides.fig_caption: Homeowners insurance premiums in 2025, up from $113.9B in 2021
slides.sub: A new consumer-group analysis of five years of NAIC data finds claims growth lagging far behind.

slides.label: paid in claims per *premium dollar*
slides.body: That was the 2025 figure, down from about 69 cents in 2021. The report puts the industry loss ratio at 68.8% in 2021 and 55.1% in 2025.

slides.title: Change from *2021 to 2025*
slides.note: Meanwhile, payouts *fell 23%* in Texas and 67% in Florida.

slides.title: What owners *run into*
points: About *30%* of claims were closed with no payment, 2021 to 2025.
More than *22%* of claims took over 60 days to pay.
Premiums rose at least 50% in five years in 19 of 30 metros (Zillow and Thumbtack data).

slides.title: Quote insurance *first*
slides.body: In Houston, Phoenix, Denver and Nashville, owners now pay more each year for insurance than for property taxes. Get buyers real quotes early so the payment holds up at closing.
